record.summary: Non-binding national guidelines built on four pillars (Fairness, Accountability, Inclusiveness and Integrity, Responsibility) that accompany the National AI Strategy. They apply across sectors and the whole AI lifecycle, including systems from external providers, and set a risk-based governance model with indicative low, medium, high and unacceptable-risk tiers, escalation controls and safeguards, data-protection alignment, transparency, explainability and human oversight, accountability, auditability and record-keeping, procurement and vendor governance, and guidance on generative, foundation and agentic AI. They are to inform sector rules and future legislation where risk justifies it.
record.notes: Cabinet agreed on 13 February 2026 to adopt the national AI strategy, AI for Mauritius, as the national guiding policy framework, supported by the FAIR guideline document, and stated that the guidelines will evolve into AI regulations as the ecosystem matures. The strategy and the guidelines were launched on 9 April 2026 at the J & J Auditorium in Phoenix (the ministry's release of 10 April 2026 says 'launched yesterday'). The guidelines state that they are not a law and create no legal obligations, and they do not apply to AI used for military, defence, national security or counter-terrorism purposes.

The PDF confirms the title, the ministry, the non-binding character, the scope, the risk tiers, the scope exclusion and the legal trajectory; the release confirms the launch 'yesterday' (9 April 2026) and that the ministry's AI Unit led the work; the Cabinet highlights (item 6) confirm the adoption of the strategy 'AI for Mauritius' supported by the FAIR guideline document and that the guidelines will evolve into AI regulations. The PDF carries no date, so date_published rests on the ministry's release. pmo.govmu.org is not yet on the list of official sites, so the Cabinet quotes count as secondary until a person records the host. The same PDF is also hosted at mitci.govmu.org as 'FINAL-GUIDELINES-15AVRIL.pdf'.

judgment.status_reasoning: Non-binding guidelines launched on 9 April 2026 and still hosted by the AI Unit; nothing stored shows them withdrawn or replaced. Published (non-binding, current).
judgment.scope_reasoning: National AI-specific governance guidelines with a risk-based model, human oversight and guidance on generative and agentic AI; in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: The PDF carries no date. The ministry's release is dated 10 April 2026 (page heading 'April 10, 2026' and closing line 'Dated 10th of April 2026') and says the strategy and guidelines were 'officially launched yesterday', so the launch and publication date is 9 April 2026. The Cabinet decision of 13 February 2026 adopted the strategy with the supporting guideline document; the published record takes the launch, when the guidelines were made public, as date_published, and the Cabinet date stays in notes.
judgment.topics_reasoning: The published topics are supported: risk-based classification (indicative risk tiers), human oversight and transparency & labelling (transparency, explainability and human oversight section), accountability & liability (accountability, auditability and record-keeping), general-purpose / frontier AI (generative, foundation and agentic AI section). Left unchanged.
judgment.issuing_body_reasoning: The cover names the ministry; the release says its AI Unit led the work; the Cabinet highlights of 13 February 2026 (item 6) record Cabinet's adoption of the strategy with the supporting FAIR guideline document, which supports 'adopted by Cabinet'. pmo.govmu.org is not on the official-sites list, so that quote counts as secondary for now.
